editorial:
Imagine being stuck on a lonely farm in the 1600s with a husband who treats you like dirt. That is exactly where you find Fanny. She spends her days trying to keep her head down and take care of her little boy while dealing with John, a man who loves control. The mood is heavy and tense from the start, making you feel the pressure Fanny is under. Everything changes when a young couple, Thomas and Rebecca, show up at the door claiming they were robbed. They seem nice at first, but you can tell pretty quickly that something is off. It turns the quiet farm into a place where you never know who to trust.

What really makes this work is the acting; you can feel the tension in every room. The plot moves slowly at first, but it builds up to some shocking moments that will keep you guessing. While it might feel a bit slow for some, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy period dramas with a dark twist, you should definitely check this one out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you love the look of old England, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The truth comes out that the visitors aren't victims, but people with their own dark secrets and agendas. After a lot of fighting and betrayal, Fanny finally finds the strength to stand up to her cruel husband. She manages to escape her miserable life and the cycle of abuse. The movie ends with her finally being free from John's control, showing that she has survived the nightmare and can start over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers set in the past.
